smell: resolve() is keyed only by trackernet_code, but app.data.trackernet_codes' own postcondition states circle and hammersmith-city both map to the same code "H", so the resolver has no way to tell which of the two lines a given RawDelayEstimate actually belongs to.
improvement_instruction: Either give resolve() a way to disambiguate estimates for lines that share a trackernet_code (e.g. only accept records whose closest_station_id_to_arrival/current_location resolve to a station or edge that is exclusive to the requested line's layout, dropping ones that fall on track shared with the other line), or, if disambiguation truly isn't possible from the feed, make the shared-code limitation an explicit precondition/postcondition of resolve() (e.g. "When trackernet_code is 'H', returned delay_minutes may include trains actually running on the other H-coded line") so callers and the frontend are not presented with per-line figures that are silently pooled across two lines.
reason: When a user opens the live map for the circle line on a station/edge that circle physically shares with hammersmith-city (most of the route), because delay_estimate_resolver's contract and trackernet_codes' aliasing of both lines to "H" are never reconciled anywhere in the design, hammersmith-city train delays get silently folded into the circle line's delay_minutes (and vice versa) even though each module's own postconditions look satisfied in isolation, producing incorrect on-screen delay figures that unit tests written against either module alone would never catch.
